expectations.text: Uses `git-stack --push` (a flag on the top-level command), not a `git-stack push` subcommand
Explains only the root/bottom branch (feature-a) is 'ready'; branches stacked on other dev branches are held back
expectations.evidence: Attributes feature-c's hold-back to push ordering, not the stacking-on-dev-branch rule, and claims that after rewording feature-b "all three branches should now show as ready" — contradicting the rule that branches stacked on dev branches are held back.

expectations.text: Identifies the 'WIP:' commit on feature-b as a blocker and suggests rewording/finishing it
expectations.evidence: "feature-b is held back because its top commit is titled 'WIP'"; suggests `git-stack reword` to drop the WIP prefix.

expectations.text: Recommends one-PR-at-a-time strategy and/or setting each gh PR base to the branch below it (not all onto main)
expectations.evidence: Each `gh pr create --base` targets the branch below it (feature-a base main, feature-b base feature-a, feature-c base feature-b).

summary: WIP blocker and stacked PR bases correct, but incorrectly claims rewording makes all stacked branches ready.
